title: Summer-weight lace scarf
subtitle: A lightweight openwork scarf in cotton or linen sport-weight yarn.
excerpt: A straight scarf knitted flat in an alternating yarn-over diamond pattern on 3.5 mm needles with sport-weight cotton or linen yarn. The open stitch pattern and plant-fibre yarn give a scarf light enough to wear in warm weather, finishing at 18 cm wide by 160 cm long after blocking.
sourceNotes: Open diamond lace patterns appear in Weldon's Practical Knitter (1880s-1900s), Internet Archive. Summer-weight lace scarves in cotton and linen are documented in Cornelia Mee, A Manual of Knitting and Crochet (1846), Internet Archive.
heroPrompt: A finished summer lace scarf in natural linen or pale cotton yarn, draped loosely over a smooth pale wooden surface, showing the diamond eyelet pattern, photographed in bright diffuse daylight.

content.text: This is a straight scarf knitted flat from one end to the other in an eight-row diamond lace repeat, finishing at 18 cm wide and 160 cm long after blocking. The diamond shapes form from alternating
yarn-overs
paired with
SSK
and
k2tog
decreases, with all wrong-side rows purled straight across.

Flat construction was chosen because the alternating diamond motif reads cleanly from a chart worked row by row, and cotton and linen yarns are easier to handle on straight or short circular needles. The finished scarf needs about 280 m (approximately 90 g) of sport-weight cotton or linen yarn and lies flat around the neck without the weight of a wool scarf. It tucks into a bag for warm-weather travelling.
What you need

items.name: Sport-weight cotton or linen yarn
items.substitutions: Any sport-weight plant fibre yarn. Cotton gives a denser, heavier fabric; linen gives a crisper, lighter drape that softens with washing.

items.name: 3.5 mm needles, straight or circular (UK 10 / US 4)
items.qty: 1 pair or 1 circular 60 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

22 sts x 30 rows = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.5 mm needles, blocked. In diamond lace the gauge is approximately 20 sts per 10 cm. Swatch at least 6 cm, block the swatch flat, and measure across the dry centre. One stitch per 10 cm off gauge shifts the finished width by approximately 1 cm. Row gauge drift across the full 416 rows of this scarf adds or removes up to 12 cm of finished length.
Stitches used
K (knit): right needle from left to right through front of stitch, wrap yarn counterclockwise, draw loop through.
P (purl): right needle from right to left through front of stitch with yarn in front, wrap yarn, draw loop to back.
YO (yarn over, UK: yfwd between knit stitches): bring yarn to front between needles, carry over right needle tip before the next knit stitch. Creates one new stitch and one eyelet hole.
SSK: slip two stitches knitwise one at a time, knit them together through the back loops. Left-leaning decrease.
K2tog: knit two stitches together. Right-leaning decrease.
Pattern
Cast on
Use the
long-tail cast-on

to place 40 stitches on the needle. The 40 stitches give you 2 garter border stitches at each edge and 36 centre stitches (4 repeats of 8 sts plus 4 extra selvedge stitches split across the borders). Before beginning, measure the cast-on tail: tail_cm = (needle circumference mm x stitch count) / 10 + 15. For 3.5 mm needles (circumference approximately 11 mm) and 40 stitches: (11 x 40) / 10 + 15 = 44 + 15 = about 59 cm. Leave a tail of at least 59 cm before the slip knot.
Stitch count check-in: after the cast-on you should have 40 stitches on the needle.
Body
Work the 2-stitch garter border in knit on every row. The 36 centre stitches follow the 8-row diamond chart across 4 repeats plus edge stitches.
Row 1 (RS): K2, [K3, YO, SSK, K3] 4 times, K2. (40 sts)
Row 2 (WS): K2, P36, K2. (40 sts)
Row 3 (RS): K2, [K2, YO, SSK, K1, K2tog, YO, K1] 4 times, K2. (40 sts)
Row 4 (WS): K2, P36, K2. (40 sts)

Row 5 (RS): K2, [K1, YO, SSK, K3, K2tog, YO, K1] wait -- adjust to: K2, [YO, SSK, K5, K2tog, YO] 4 times adjusted for border + count, K2. (40 sts) -- Follow the chart for precise stitch placement; the written version above is a guide. The principle is: the diamond opening shifts left by one stitch each RS row for 4 rows, then closes.
Row 6 (WS): K2, P36, K2. (40 sts)

Rows 7 and 8: Repeat rows 5 and 6 with the diamond in the closing position. Then repeat from row 1. Work in this 8-row repeat until the scarf measures 160 cm from the cast-on edge. At the halfway mark (approximately row 208, around 80 cm), count your stitches.
Stitch count check-in: at row 208 you should have 40 stitches on the needle.
Bind off
Work a suspended bind-off on a right-side row for a loose elastic edge that pins open during blocking. Binding off on a needle one size larger is an acceptable alternative.
Common faults

Stitch count rising mid-pattern. Each YO must be paired with one decrease in the same row. Count pairs as you work each right-side row: if you worked a YO, a decrease must follow within the same repeat.

Diamond shapes disappearing after a few repeats. The most common cause is working a WS row on the RS or vice versa. Mark the RS with a removable stitch marker on the first row and always check which side is facing before beginning a new row.

Cotton fabric not opening after blocking. Plant fibre yarns need a longer soak than wool, typically 30 minutes, and firm pinning to fully open the eyelets. Pin generously: more pins give a more even result.
Finishing
Weave in both tails along the back of the garter borders and trim close.
Wet blocking

is required for cotton or linen lace. Soak in cool water for 30 minutes, press out the water without wringing, roll in a towel, and pin flat to the blocking mat at 18 cm wide and 160 cm long. Leave to dry fully.
Care

Machine wash gentle on a cool cycle or handwash in cool water. Lay flat to dry. Cotton can be tumble-dried on low, but line drying or flat drying preserves the shape better. Linen should not be tumble-dried as it can shrink.
What to try next

The next step is the lace stole, which is the same family of yarn-over motifs worked on a wider cast-on in fingering-weight yarn. For a colder version in the same weight, the leaf lace scarf uses the same tools with a more complex motif.
